-- From the CcNoc router (XBlue/Examples/CcNoc/Router.lean): the matrix
-- arbiter that picks which input port may use an output port. Bit 3*i+j of
-- `pb` says "requester i is above requester j". The winner is the requester
-- that no other requester is above; it then drops below everyone.
xblue module mkMatrixArbiter3;
  input Bool reset;
  input Bit#(3) req;
  -- after reset: 0 above 1 above 2 (diagonal 0)
  Reg#(Bit#(9)) pb <- mkReg(0x0ee);

  -- requester `idx` may go if no requester above it asks
  function Bool permit(Bit#(3) r, Integer idx) =
    (r & { (2 > idx ? ~pb[idx * 3 + 2] : pb[2 * 3 + idx]),
           (1 > idx ? ~pb[idx * 3 + 1] : pb[1 * 3 + idx]),
           (0 > idx ? ~pb[idx * 3 + 0] : pb[0 * 3 + idx]) }) == 0;
  Bit#(2) winner = (req[2] && permit(req, 2)) ? 2 : ((req[1] && permit(req, 1)) ? 1 : 0);

  method Bit#(3) io_grant = req == 0 ? 0 : (3'b001 << winner);

  -- the winner goes to the bottom: its row is cleared, its column set
  rule update (req != 0);
    for (Integer i = 0; i < 3; i = i + 1)
      for (Integer j = 0; j < 3; j = j + 1)
        pb[i * 3 + j : i * 3 + j] <= winner == i ? 1'b0 : (winner == j ? 1'b1 : pb[i * 3 + j]);
  endrule
  rule clear (reset);
    pb <= 0x0ee;
  endrule
  schedule update ≫ clear;
endmodule
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------- reasoning
open XBlue

/-- One clock cycle of the design itself: the grant it shows, and the next matrix. -/
def next (reset : BitVec 1) (req : BitVec 3) (pb : BitVec 9) : BitVec 3 × BitVec 9 :=
  let s := mkMatrixArbiter3.design.cycle (.cons reset (.cons req .nil)) (.cons pb .nil)
  (s.wires.get mkMatrixArbiter3.io_grant, s.regs.get mkMatrixArbiter3.pb)

/-- "j is above i", as the design reads it: for j < i the bit (j, i); for j > i
    the complement of the bit (i, j); for j = i the diagonal bit. -/
def above (pb : BitVec 9) (j i : Nat) : Bool :=
  if j < i then pb.getLsbD (3 * j + i) else if i < j then !pb.getLsbD (3 * i + j) else pb.getLsbD (4 * i)

/-- Requester i wins when it asks and no asking requester is above it. -/
def wins (pb : BitVec 9) (req : BitVec 3) (i : Nat) : Bool :=
  req.getLsbD i && !(req.getLsbD 0 && above pb 0 i) && !(req.getLsbD 1 && above pb 1 i) &&
    !(req.getLsbD 2 && above pb 2 i)

def winner (pb : BitVec 9) (req : BitVec 3) : BitVec 2 :=
  if wins pb req 2 then 2#2 else if wins pb req 1 then 1#2 else 0#2

/-- The winner goes to the bottom: its row is cleared, its column is set. -/
def row (w : BitVec 2) : BitVec 9 := if w = 0#2 then 0b000000111#9 else if w = 1#2 then 0b000111000#9 else 0b111000000#9

def col (w : BitVec 2) : BitVec 9 := if w = 0#2 then 0b001001001#9 else if w = 1#2 then 0b010010010#9 else 0b100100100#9

def update (pb : BitVec 9) (w : BitVec 2) : BitVec 9 := (pb ||| col w) &&& ~~~row w

-- One plain function per step of the cycle.
def grantStep (req : BitVec 3) (pb : BitVec 9) : BitVec 3 :=          -- interfaces
  if req = 0#3 then 0#3 else if winner pb req = 2#2 then 4#3 else if winner pb req = 1#2 then 2#3 else 1#3
def updateStep (req : BitVec 3) (pb : BitVec 9) : BitVec 9 :=         -- update
  if req = 0#3 then pb else update pb (winner pb req)
def clearStep (reset : BitVec 1) (pb : BitVec 9) : BitVec 9 :=        -- clear
  if reset = 1#1 then 0x0ee#9 else pb

/-- The cycle: show the grant, then `update`, then `clear`. -/
theorem next_eq_steps (reset : BitVec 1) (req : BitVec 3) (pb : BitVec 9) :
    next reset req pb = (grantStep req pb, clearStep reset (updateStep req pb)) := by
  -- unfold the design's cycle
  simp [next, mkMatrixArbiter3.design, Design.cycle,
    mkMatrixArbiter3.schedule, mkMatrixArbiter3.interfaces, mkMatrixArbiter3.rules.update,
    mkMatrixArbiter3.rules.clear, mkMatrixArbiter3.values.winner, mkMatrixArbiter3.signature,
    Sched.run, Action.step, Action.fires, writesIf, State.write, State.cur, State.read, HList.set,
    HList.get, Expr.eval, Expr.binVal, Expr.cmpVal, Common.putR, Common.putW, Common.memAt,
    mkMatrixArbiter3.pb, mkMatrixArbiter3.reset, mkMatrixArbiter3.req, mkMatrixArbiter3.io_grant, sliceWidth]
  -- name the three steps
  simp only [grantStep, updateStep, clearStep, winner, wins, above, update, row, col]
  -- the design shifts `1` left by the winner's index
  have hs : ∀ w : BitVec 2, 1#3 <<< (w.toNat % 8) =
      (if w = 2#2 then 4#3 else if w = 1#2 then 2#3 else if w = 0#2 then 1#3 else 0#3) := by decide
  simp only [hs]
  bv_decide

/-- Fairness: the winner goes below everyone, so while anyone else asks it
    cannot win again. -/
theorem winner_waits (pb : BitVec 9) (req : BitVec 3) (w : BitVec 2) (j : Fin 3)
    (hw : w ≠ 3#2) (hj : j.val ≠ w.toNat) (hr : req.getLsbD j = true) :
    wins (update pb w) req w.toNat = false := by
  have h3 : ∀ v : BitVec 2, v ≠ 3#2 → v = 0#2 ∨ v = 1#2 ∨ v = 2#2 := by decide
  rcases h3 w hw with rfl | rfl | rfl <;> fin_cases j <;>
    simp_all [wins, above, update, row, col]

/-- The cycle-level version: after a grant, the winner cannot win again while
    another requester asks. -/
theorem no_repeat (pb : BitVec 9) (req : BitVec 3) (h : req ≠ 0#3) (j : Fin 3)
    (hj : j.val ≠ (winner pb req).toNat) (hr : req.getLsbD j = true) :
    wins (next 0#1 req pb).2 req (winner pb req).toNat = false := by
  have h3 : winner pb req ≠ 3#2 := by
    unfold winner; split <;> (try split) <;> decide
  rw [next_eq_steps]
  simp only [clearStep, updateStep, h, if_false]
  simpa using winner_waits pb req _ j h3 hj hr

-- From the CcNoc router (XBlue/Examples/CcNoc/Router.lean): the matrix
-- arbiter that picks which input port may use an output port. Bit 3*i+j of
-- `pb` says "requester i is above requester j". The winner is the requester
-- that no other requester is above; it then drops below everyone.
xblue module mkMatrixArbiter3;
  input Bool reset;
  input Bit#(3) req;
  -- after reset: 0 above 1 above 2 (diagonal 0)
  Reg#(Bit#(9)) pb <- mkReg(0x0ee);

  -- requester `idx` may go if no requester above it asks
  function Bool permit(Bit#(3) r, Integer idx) =
    (r & { (2 > idx ? ~pb[idx * 3 + 2] : pb[2 * 3 + idx]),
           (1 > idx ? ~pb[idx * 3 + 1] : pb[1 * 3 + idx]),
           (0 > idx ? ~pb[idx * 3 + 0] : pb[0 * 3 + idx]) }) == 0;
  Bit#(2) winner = (req[2] && permit(req, 2)) ? 2 : ((req[1] && permit(req, 1)) ? 1 : 0);

  method Bit#(3) io_grant = req == 0 ? 0 : (3'b001 << winner);

  -- the winner goes to the bottom: its row is cleared, its column set
  rule update (req != 0);
    for (Integer i = 0; i < 3; i = i + 1)
      for (Integer j = 0; j < 3; j = j + 1)
        pb[i * 3 + j : i * 3 + j] <= winner == i ? 1'b0 : (winner == j ? 1'b1 : pb[i * 3 + j]);
  endrule
  rule clear (reset);
    pb <= 0x0ee;
  endrule
  schedule update ≫ clear;
endmodule

def next (reset : BitVec 1) (req : BitVec 3) (pb : BitVec 9) : BitVec 3 × BitVec 9 :=
  let s := mkMatrixArbiter3.design.cycle (.cons reset (.cons req .nil)) (.cons pb .nil)
  (s.wires.get mkMatrixArbiter3.io_grant, s.regs.get mkMatrixArbiter3.pb)

/-- "j is above i", as the design reads it: for j < i the bit (j, i); for j > i
    the complement of the bit (i, j); for j = i the diagonal bit. -/
def above (pb : BitVec 9) (j i : Nat) : Bool :=
  if j < i then pb.getLsbD (3 * j + i) else if i < j then !pb.getLsbD (3 * i + j) else pb.getLsbD (4 * i)

/-- Requester i wins when it asks and no asking requester is above it. -/
def wins (pb : BitVec 9) (req : BitVec 3) (i : Nat) : Bool :=
  req.getLsbD i && !(req.getLsbD 0 && above pb 0 i) && !(req.getLsbD 1 && above pb 1 i) &&
    !(req.getLsbD 2 && above pb 2 i)

def winner (pb : BitVec 9) (req : BitVec 3) : BitVec 2 :=
  if wins pb req 2 then 2#2 else if wins pb req 1 then 1#2 else 0#2

/-- The winner goes to the bottom: its row is cleared, its column is set. -/
def row (w : BitVec 2) : BitVec 9 := if w = 0#2 then 0b000000111#9 else if w = 1#2 then 0b000111000#9 else 0b111000000#9

def col (w : BitVec 2) : BitVec 9 := if w = 0#2 then 0b001001001#9 else if w = 1#2 then 0b010010010#9 else 0b100100100#9

def update (pb : BitVec 9) (w : BitVec 2) : BitVec 9 := (pb ||| col w) &&& ~~~row w

explain: In a reset cycle with requests: 1. clear runs first: pb = 0xee. 2. update runs and computes the winner of that matrix (0) and moves it to the bottom: pb = 0xe8. So pb leaves reset with one grant already applied. The reset at cycle 9 shows it: the original has pb = 0xee at cycle 10 (and grants 1, 2 from there), the swapped one has 0xe8.

-/-- One clock cycle of the design itself: the grant it shows, and the next matrix. -/
-def next (reset : BitVec 1) (req : BitVec 3) (pb : BitVec 9) : BitVec 3 × BitVec 9 :=
-  let s := mkMatrixArbiter3.design.cycle (.cons reset (.cons req .nil)) (.cons pb .nil)
-  (s.wires.get mkMatrixArbiter3.io_grant, s.regs.get mkMatrixArbiter3.pb)
-/-- "j is above i", as the design reads it: for j < i the bit (j, i); for j > i
-    the complement of the bit (i, j); for j = i the diagonal bit. -/
-def above (pb : BitVec 9) (j i : Nat) : Bool :=
-  if j < i then pb.getLsbD (3 * j + i) else if i < j then !pb.getLsbD (3 * i + j) else pb.getLsbD (4 * i)
-/-- Requester i wins when it asks and no asking requester is above it. -/
-def wins (pb : BitVec 9) (req : BitVec 3) (i : Nat) : Bool :=
-  req.getLsbD i && !(req.getLsbD 0 && above pb 0 i) && !(req.getLsbD 1 && above pb 1 i) &&
-    !(req.getLsbD 2 && above pb 2 i)
-def winner (pb : BitVec 9) (req : BitVec 3) : BitVec 2 :=
-  if wins pb req 2 then 2#2 else if wins pb req 1 then 1#2 else 0#2
-/-- The winner goes to the bottom: its row is cleared, its column is set. -/
-def row (w : BitVec 2) : BitVec 9 := if w = 0#2 then 0b000000111#9 else if w = 1#2 then 0b000111000#9 else 0b111000000#9
-def col (w : BitVec 2) : BitVec 9 := if w = 0#2 then 0b001001001#9 else if w = 1#2 then 0b010010010#9 else 0b100100100#9
-def update (pb : BitVec 9) (w : BitVec 2) : BitVec 9 := (pb ||| col w) &&& ~~~row w

-def grantStep (req : BitVec 3) (pb : BitVec 9) : BitVec 3 :=          -- interfaces
-  if req = 0#3 then 0#3 else if winner pb req = 2#2 then 4#3 else if winner pb req = 1#2 then 2#3 else 1#3

-  if req = 0#3 then pb else update pb (winner pb req)
-def clearStep (reset : BitVec 1) (pb : BitVec 9) : BitVec 9 :=        -- clear
-  if reset = 1#1 then 0x0ee#9 else pb
